claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the compared quaternary and ternary subsets can all be prepared as single-phase FCC materials by identical thermomechanical processing.
Mechanical-property differences among these alloys are not explained simply by constituent count.
The full quinary alloy has enhanced local lattice distortion relative to its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Local elemental clustering is present only in the full quinary system.
Local lattice distortions act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Local elemental clusters or short-range chemical order act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The accumulation of atomic-size mismatches and chemical interactions among five elements produces local lattice distortions and nanoscale elemental clusters.
The disparate atomic sizes in the quinary alloy induce greater lattice distortion.
The combination of five constituent elements favors formation of nanometer-scale clusters.
Lattice distortion and nanoscale clusters impede dislocation movement more effectively in the quinary alloy than in the quaternary or ternary variants.
Quaternary and ternary variants have less pronounced lattice strain because of their lower compositional complexity.
Quaternary and ternary variants have less pronounced elemental clustering because of their lower compositional complexity.
The quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower yield strengths than the quinary baseline.
The quaternary and ternary alloys will have work-hardening rates different from those of the quinary baseline.
The quinary alloy will have higher yield strength because its enhanced lattice distortion and clustering create a more effective obstacle field.
The proposed relationships apply to single-phase FCC specimens with matched processing, grain size, geometry, and room-temperature tensile-test conditions.
High-resolution diffraction can be used to compare lattice distortion, while atom-probe tomography or TEM can be used to compare elemental clustering in the alloy series.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says local elemental clustering is present only in the full quinary system, whereas the mechanism says quaternary and ternary alloys have less pronounced clustering, implying that clustering is present in those alloys as well.
